title: Russian Attacks on Ukrainian Targets Escalate Tensions in Capital
seoTitle: Russian Attacks on Ukraine Targets Escalate Capital.
subtitle: Russian Drones Hit Security Service Building and Coca-Cola Facility in Kyiv
excerpt: Russian drones struck Ukraine's Security Service headquarters and a Coca-Cola factory near Kyiv, raising new concerns about escalation.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Folha de S.Paulo, G1, Gazeta do Povo
contentHtml:
Last Friday, September 4, Russia carried out two drone attacks that drew global attention: one hit the headquarters of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) in Kyiv, and another set fire to a Coca-Cola factory on the outskirts of the capital. These incidents marked the first time the SBU building was directly targeted since the war began in 2022.

The SBU Attack in Kyiv

A drone was launched against the building located on Volodymyrska Street, opposite St. Sophia Cathedral, striking the office of the interim head of the agency, Oleksandr Poklad. President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that the official was not on site at the time of the explosion and that five people were injured, with two others hospitalized. Emergency teams were immediately mobilized.

Ukrainian Reaction to the SBU Attack

Zelensky ordered Poklad to prepare an “adequate and concrete” response to the attack, emphasizing that the Ukrainian Armed Forces would support the retaliatory action. The president also thanked the emergency services and highlighted the need for assistance to the victims.

Coca-Cola Factory Fire

On Thursday, September 3, Russian Shahed drones struck a Coca-Cola factory near the city of Brovary, east of Kyiv. According to President Zelensky, the target was chosen because the company represents “such a big enemy.” No workers were injured, but the attack caused a plume of smoke and material damage that is being assessed by authorities and Coca-Cola itself.

International Repercussions of the Coca-Cola Attack

Zelensky stated that the attack sent a “clear signal” to the United States, emphasizing that the factory, as an American facility, could not be ignored. Andy Hunder, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Ukraine, confirmed that no employees were injured and that the company is collaborating with authorities to assess the damages.

Context of Escalating Air Attacks

The two incidents occur amid an intensification of Russian bombardments over the Ukrainian capital. According to CNN, at least 53 people have died and 134 have been injured in Kyiv and the metropolitan region since the beginning of last month's offensive. The increased frequency of attacks on government buildings and civilian infrastructure raises the risk of more casualties and amplifies diplomatic pressures for possible international mediation.

With information from Folha de S.Paulo, G1, Gazeta do Povo.
